<objective>
Assemble the **observe-only supervisor daemon** — the integration point of Phase 19. It composes
plan 01's bridge reader + plan 02's registry resolver into the full detect loop and proves the two
safety properties (PILOT-05): the `cco-dream` boundary seam (D-16) and disk-persisted idempotency
(D-15). It takes NO action — it logs structured `would_*` decisions only (D-12), mirroring
`cco-dream --dry-run`. Acting is the flag Phase 20 introduces.

Purpose:
- PILOT-02 (core) — the poll loop + the operator-tailable JSONL action log (what / which session / when / why).
- PILOT-05 — every would-be `claude -p` is built as a `cco-dream` subprocess argv (never raw `claude -p`,
  never `--dangerously-skip-permissions`); the daemon never double-fires the same action on the same
  session/event (idempotent, restart-surviving).

Output: `daemon.py` + `runner.py` + `idempotency.py`, all GREEN under fixtures. The launchd plist,
the `~/.zshrc` wrapper, the tmux install, and the LIVE `cco-dream` probe are plan 04.

<!-- Contracts this plan CONSUMES (from plans 01/02) and the cco-dream argv it COMPOSES. -->

From autopilot/bridge.py (plan 01):
```python
read_bridge(session_id, *, tmpdir=None) -> Optional[dict]   # {used_pct, timestamp, …} or None
discover_sessions(*, tmpdir=None) -> list[str]              # live session_ids (excludes *-nudged)
is_stale(bridge, *, now) -> bool                            # now - timestamp > 60
STALE_SECONDS = 60
```
From autopilot/registry.py (plan 02):
```python
resolve_pane(session_id, *, registry_dir) -> Optional[str]  # the %N pane, or None if unmapped
reconcile(records, live_panes, *, live_sessions) -> dict
tmux_live_panes(*, run=subprocess.run) -> set
read_registry(*, registry_dir) -> dict
```

`cco-dream` is the byte-stable safety boundary (md5 d8055242bffbee5cb3ea557340c6a444 — DO NOT EDIT IT).
It is a BASH script at `~/.claude/bin/cco-dream`. VERIFIED facts about its CLI (from reading it):
- REQUIRES `--metric '<cmd>'` AND `--surface <git-repo-path>` (the surface MUST be a git repo).
- Has `--dry-run` (validate config + worktree + green-check ONCE, runs NO `claude -p`, NO commit — the
  safe smoke path) and `--max-cost USD`.
- NEVER passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; its built-in `--disallowedTools` denylist is
  `Bash(rm *) Bash(sudo *) Bash(dd *) Bash(mkfs *) Bash(chmod *) Bash(chown *) Bash(shutdown *) Bash(reboot *) Bash(diskutil *) Bash(launchctl *)`.
- So the Phase-19 "benign no-op probe" (D-16) is `cco-dream --metric <noop> --surface <throwaway-git> --dry-run`
  — it proves the seam WITHOUT any keystroke and WITHOUT any real `claude -p`. The daemon BUILDS this argv
  (this plan, unit-tested via the stub); plan 04 RUNS it once against the live binary.

The bridge timestamp is epoch SECONDS; staleness gate = 60s. The 60% trigger evaluated (but NOT acted on)
this phase: `used_pct >= 60` ⇒ decision `would_compact`. Other decisions: `stale_skip` (bridge >60s old),
`unmapped` (no pane in the registry), `no_op` (fresh + under 60%).
</interfaces>

    - `evaluate_session(session_id, *, now, tmpdir, registry_dir, state_dir, threshold=60)` → dict (the JSONL event,
      NOT sent anywhere). Logic, in order:
      1. bridge = read_bridge(session_id) — None → decision `no_op` reason "no_bridge".
      2. is_stale(bridge, now=now) → decision `stale_skip` reason "bridge>60s" (NEVER acts on stale — PILOT-04).
      3. pane = resolve_pane(session_id) — None → decision `unmapped` reason "no_pane".
      4. used = bridge["used_pct"]; if used < threshold → `no_op` reason "under_threshold".
      5. used >= threshold: if already_fired(session_id,"compact") → `no_op` reason "already_armed";
         else record_fired(...) and decision `would_compact` (OBSERVE-ONLY — log only; NO keystroke, NO cco-dream call).
      6. Re-arm: when used < threshold AND a prior arming exists → clear_fired (so the next crossing re-fires).
      Every event dict = `{ts, session_id, pane, cwd, used_pct, decision, reason}` (cwd from the registry record).
    - `poll_once(*, now, tmpdir, registry_dir, state_dir, log_path)`: discover_sessions → reconcile against
      `tmux_live_panes` + live_sessions → evaluate each → APPEND one JSON line per event to log_path.

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| would-be `claude -p` → the system | Any process the daemon would ever spawn to drive Claude is the highest-risk surface (arbitrary tool use under an unattended daemon). |
| bridge/registry data → a fire decision | Stale or forged bridge data, or a dangling registry record, could drive a wrong/duplicate action. |
| poll loop → daemon liveness | One malformed input must not kill the always-on daemon. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-19-09 | Elevation of privilege | the would-be `claude -p` path | mitigate | The ONLY path to `claude -p` is `runner.build_cco_dream_argv`, which routes through the byte-stable `cco-dream` boundary (its `--disallowedTools` denylist + pre-flight catastrophe check) and is structurally incapable of adding `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (D-16, RUNNER-01/02). Tested: argv assertion. This phase only BUILDS a `--dry-run` probe (no real `claude -p`). |
| T-19-10 | Tampering (command injection) | cco-dream / future send-keys argv | mitigate | All subprocess invocation is argv-LIST (never `shell=True`) — bridge/registry values are passed as discrete args, never interpolated into a shell string. Verified: `grep shell=True` returns nothing across the package. |
| T-19-11 | Spoofing (stale/forged data → wrong action) | `evaluate_session` | mitigate | The 60s staleness gate (`stale_skip`) + the D-10 reconcile (drop dead-pane/no-bridge records before evaluating) mean a stale bridge or a dangling registry entry yields `stale_skip`/`unmapped`, never a `would_compact` on a dead session. Tested. |
| T-19-12 | Repudiation / double-action | idempotency state | mitigate | Per-`(session_id,event)` disk state (atomic temp+rename) makes `would_compact` fire once per crossing and survive a KeepAlive restart (D-15). Tested across a simulated restart. |
| T-19-13 | DoS (daemon crash-loop) | the `main` poll loop | mitigate | The loop body is wrapped in `except Exception as e:` that logs + continues (never a bare except) so one bad poll/input can't kill the daemon; launchd `ThrottleInterval` (plan 04) caps any restart rate. |
</threat_model>
